items.prompt:
Two authors can agree on the same facts but differ in their:
A) interpretation or emphasis
B) spelling only
C) page count

steps: Same facts, different takes. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Reading multiple authors on one topic helps you get a:
A) fuller, more balanced understanding
B) narrower view
C) list of titles

steps: Multiple views = balance. Key is A.

items.prompt:
An author shapes their presentation by choosing which ____ to emphasize.
A) evidence
B) fonts
C) page numbers

steps: Selection shapes framing. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Two articles both say a factory will create 500 jobs. One stresses the jobs; the other stresses the pollution. They differ in:
A) the facts
B) what they emphasize
C) nothing

steps: Same facts, different emphasis. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Two historians agree a battle happened but disagree on how important it was. They differ in their:
A) interpretation
B) dates
C) spelling

steps: Different meaning of facts. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Why is it useful to read SEVERAL authors on a controversial topic?
A) to see different emphases and interpretations and judge for yourself
B) to copy one author
C) to avoid thinking
items.answer: A) to see different emphases and interpretations and judge for yourself

solution.answer: A) to see different emphases and interpretations and judge for yourself

items.prompt:
One author describes a protest as 'a passionate call for justice'; another calls it 'a disruptive disturbance.' They:
A) report different facts
B) interpret and frame the same event very differently
C) agree completely
items.answer: B) interpret and frame the same event very differently

steps: Different framing of one event. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) interpret and frame the same event very differently

items.prompt:
Two science writers cite the SAME study but one concludes the new drug is 'a breakthrough' and the other 'needs more testing.' A careful reader should:
A) note they interpret the same evidence differently and look for more information
B) trust whichever sounds nicer
C) assume one is lying
items.answer: A) note they interpret the same evidence differently and look for more information

steps: Same data, different interpretation. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) note they interpret the same evidence differently and look for more information
